proposals.relationship: Morgan uses Pocock’s reconstruction of republican political ideas to explain the connection between property,independence and liberty in Jefferson’s outlook.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1972,8/n6 and9/n9,uses Pocock’s1965Machiavelli/Harrington study alongside CarolineRobbins,and in the colonial political comparison with MichaelZuckerman/RobertWeir. These plural resources substantiate one part of the American-paradox argument,not a claim that Pocock supplied its whole slavery mechanism. Original1965essay and the other cited works remain unread.
primary_locators: Slavery and Freedom1972,printed8,paragraph beginning Though Jefferson’s concern,note6;9,Harrington/commonwealthman genealogy and note9.

proposals.relationship: Morgan credits Davis’s research suggestions while using his work to examine how opposition to African slavery could coexist with demands to enslave the idle poor.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1972,p10/n12,explicitly thanks Davis and cites Problem of Slavery in Western Culture1966,374–378,beside Hutcheson’s position. This records specific scholarly assistance and a textual resource,not the inference that Davis invented Morgan’s whole Virginia mechanism. The original Davis and Hutcheson works remain unread.
primary_locators: Slavery and Freedom1972,printed10,last paragraph and note12;10 visually collated.

proposals.relationship: Morgan uses Tawney’s New Medicine for Poverty formulation to interpret religious discipline and republican distrust of the idle poor.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1972p10 names Tawney’s formulation within the argument connecting freedom,dependency and prescribed coerced labor. It is a bounded conceptual resource,not assent to all Tawney’s economic history or proof of mentoring. This selected passage supplies no exact original Tawney work/edition;none is guessed and the original remains unread.
primary_locators: Slavery and Freedom1972,printed10,paragraph beginning That people in the lowest condition,especially religious cure for idleness.

proposals.relationship: Morgan places Weber’s interpretation of disciplined religious conduct within his explanation of republican attitudes toward poverty and compulsory labor.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1972p10 explicitly connects the religious/ethical doctrines discussed with Weber’s account of capitalism’s spirit,and then contrasts the treatment of those thought to reject that discipline. Tawney’s separate formulation retains credit. This narrow use neither endorses Weber’s complete causal thesis nor derives Morgan’s entire paradox from it. Original Weber work/edition not specified in this passage and unread.
primary_locators: Slavery and Freedom1972,printed10,Tawney/Weber paragraph immediately before note12.

proposals.relationship: Morgan uses Bailyn’s reconstruction of Commonwealthman ideas to explain the development of revolutionary American political thought.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1974review calls Bailyn’s analysis a special contribution and uses it to frame both revolutionary ideology and Hutchinson’s ordeal. It coexists with Morgan’s criticism of the biography’s paranoia framing;Robbins’s prior identification of the Commonwealthmen retains credit. Morgan’s already recorded contribution to Bailyn is a distinct reverse transmission. Bailyn’s original books and Robbins’s book unread.
primary_locators: A Loyal Un-American1974,opening paragraphs beginning After the Second World War and After thus examining;subsequent nominal/actual governor-power account.

proposals.relationship: Morgan argues that Bailyn’s sympathetic Hutchinson biography risks understating the revolutionaries’ justified fears of arbitrary power.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1974review praises meticulous research and accepts Hutchinson’s undeserved suffering,but resists making the Revolution a product of national paranoia or a witch-hunt. He points to patronage and unlimited Parliamentary authority as real dangers. This qualified criticism does not deny ideological fear or endorse Hutchinson’s persecution;it is distinct from the existing Morgan→Bailyn contribution.
primary_locators: A Loyal Un-American1974,paragraphs beginning In the concluding pages,But one learns,and But to leave it at that;final three paragraphs.

proposals.relationship: Morgan uses Berlin’s negotiated-relationship account of slavery to argue for understanding enslaved people’s cultural autonomy without reducing them to passive victims.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1998review explicitly builds this argument through Many Thousands Gone while also crediting Philip D.Morgan’s distinct Slave Counterpoint. Joint Edmund/MarieMorgan2010review again uses Berlin’s synthesis of family,culture and migration. This is a particular interpretive resource,not an assertion that Berlin originated every agency argument or that negotiation implied equal bargaining power. All original reviewed books remain unread.
primary_locators: The Big American Crime1998,paragraphs beginning Berlin,who has already contributed and Those sufferings;How Black & White America Took Shape2010,opening Berlin/ManyThousandsGone/family paragraphs.

proposals.relationship: Morgan qualifies Berlin’s reconstruction of slave culture and the presentation of testimony,questioning unsupported attributions and the risk that guilt obscures agency.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1998review distinguishes two targets:Many Thousands Gone’s African-origin/oppositional attributions may outrun sparse sources,yet its framework is praised;Remembering Slavery’s presentation may invite guilt/pity,yet the closing Faulk recollection is a corrective. Marc Favreau and Steven F.Miller share collection editing,not sole-authored Many Thousands Gone. Dialect/audio presentation is part of the latter criticism. WGBH productions are separate targets. These are Morgan’s contested interpretive judgments;original books/audio unread.
primary_locators: The Big American Crime1998,paragraph beginning One would like to know more,ending with praise of Berlin’s frame and vocabulary.
The Big American Crime1998,paragraphs beginning Readers can now find a sample,Readers in search of a guilt trip,Only toward the end,and That quotation redeems the book.

proposals.relationship: Edmund and Marie Morgan use Woodward’s account of Jim Crow’s development in interpreting the timing and pressures of African-American migration.
proposals.evidence_note: Joint2010review explicitly attributes this interpretive step to Woodward while discussing Berlin’s migration sequence. MarieMorgan retains coauthor credit. The review’s chronology is their reading,not independently verified here;no claim that this exhausts Woodward’s account or that Berlin’s whole argument derives from him. The original Woodward work is unnamed in the selected passage and unread.
primary_locators: How Black & White America Took Shape2010,paragraph beginning It was not a feature that African-Americans embraced,and explicit as C.Vann Woodward has shown attribution.
